claim: A stage variable can make API Gateway call a different backend web host per stage (for example example.com for the production endpoint and beta.example.com for the beta stage), and stage variables can specify a different AWS Lambda function name for each stage; but you can't use a stage variable to set a different integration endpoint, such as pointing a GET request to an HTTP proxy integration in one stage and a Lambda proxy integration in another stage.

evidence.quote: You can use a stage variable so that when API callers invoke your production endpoint, API Gateway calls `example.com`. Then, when API callers invoke the beta stage, API Gateway calls a different web host, such as `beta.example.com`.

Similarly, stage variables can be used to specify a different AWS Lambda function name for each stage in your API. You can't use a stage variable to set a different integration endpoint, such as pointing the `GET` request to an HTTP proxy integration in one stage and a Lambda proxy integration in another stage.
